headline: President Lee Jae Myung Appoints First Female National Intelligence Chief
seoTitle: Lee Jae Myung Appoints First Female Intelligence Chief
metaDescription: President Lee Jae Myung has nominated former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as the first female head of South Korea's National Intelligence Service.
aiSummaryBullets: President Lee Jae Myung has nominated Kang Kum-sil to serve as the new head of the National Intelligence Service.
If confirmed, the 69-year-old former justice minister would become the first woman to lead the South Korean spy agency since its founding in 1961.
The nomination is part of a broader reshuffle affecting the foreign ministry, unification ministry, and culture ministry.
aiContextParagraph: President Lee Jae Myung has announced significant changes to his security and ministerial team, most notably the selection of Kang Kum-sil to head the National Intelligence Service. Kang, who previously served as South Korea's first female justice minister, is a former judge and lawyer. Her nomination marks a potential milestone, as she would be the first woman to lead the intelligence agency since the establishment of its predecessor in 1961. This reshuffle follows recent leadership changes across government sectors, including the appointment of a new police chief. In addition to the intelligence agency nomination, the President has designated new leads for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Unification, and the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, signaling a comprehensive restructuring of his administration's high-level personnel and security architecture.
whyItIsViral: The story is trending due to significant public interest in the first-ever female appointment to lead the intelligence agency, covered by two major national outlets.
